scope: Full daily Power Stack research refresh across tracked US, Hong Kong/China, Malaysia and global ideas. Research-only. No site code, UI, scoring logic, automation logic or backend architecture changed.
executiveRead: Physical infrastructure demand remains stronger than the equity-duration backdrop. July ISM confirms accelerating US manufacturing orders/production/backlogs and persistent electrical/electronic shortages, while long-end Treasury yields near 4.7%/5.25% and elevated oil/refined-product inflation keep discount-rate pressure high. The preferred stack remains profitable power/grid/electrical bottlenecks, first-wave automation and selected energy/refining infrastructure. Speculative nuclear developers, humanoid OEMs and AI-duration names remain tactical rather than core.

macro.rates: 10Y about 4.71%; 30Y about 5.25%, with the recent 30Y high around 5.34%. Treasury buyback relief was temporary.
macro.fx: Dollar index around 98.8 and near three-month lows as fiscal/buyback concerns offset high nominal yields.
macro.energy: Brent around the mid-$93 area after a sixth straight daily gain; diesel crack previously exceeded $100/bbl and middle-distillate scarcity remains more acute than crude scarcity.
macro.risk: S&P 500 rose Friday but fell 1.4% on the week; Nasdaq fell 2.1% on the week. Duration sensitivity remains high.

ism.powerStackRead: Electrical Equipment and Computer/Electronic Products reported stronger activity while customer inventories stayed too low. Copper, electrical/electronic components, memory and semiconductors remained in short supply; services separately flagged switchgear, wire/cable and electronic components as scarce. This favours pricing-power/backlog owners but raises cost/schedule risk for contractors.
ism.sourcePolicy: Official ISM pages authoritative; only selected public respondent comments and aggregate diffusion data used. No claim of confidential/raw submissions.

categoryChanges.Power / Grid: UNCHANGED OVERWEIGHT. GEV/ETN/PWR remain strongest quality expressions. European hyperscale siting is moving toward cheaper secondary locations with faster power access, reinforcing the thesis that power availability and interconnection speed now determine data-centre geography. Higher rates increase entry discipline but do not weaken operating demand.
categoryChanges.AI / Data centres: FUNDAMENTALS STRONG, VALUATION DISCIPLINE TIGHTER. GEV data-centre orders exceed $5bn YTD; Eaton electrical orders/backlog and nVent/Vertiv growth remain exceptional. Nvidia Aug 26 is the next capex-confidence test. Prefer electrical/cooling/power over financing-heavy compute infrastructure where cash conversion is weaker.
categoryChanges.Nuclear: UNCHANGED. Existing operating assets and nuclear-component suppliers remain preferred over pre-revenue developers. BWXT/CEG/CGN Power retain stronger risk-adjusted positioning than OKLO/SMR. No new event today justifies a conviction change.
categoryChanges.Uranium / Fuel: UNCHANGED. CCJ core, LEU strategic enrichment scarcity, NXE higher-beta development satellite. No financing announcement has yet closed the remaining NXE project-funding gap; do not treat strategic discussions as completed funding.
categoryChanges.Oil & Gas: REFINING REMAINS TACTICALLY STRONGER THAN GENERIC CRUDE BETA. Global middle-distillate shortage and refinery outages continue to support VLO/MPC and integrated refiners with strong downstream. XOM/CVX/CNOOC remain high-quality broader energy exposures; WMB/KMI/LNG/PETRONAS Gas retain lower-beta infrastructure roles.
categoryChanges.Metals: COPPER STRUCTURAL THESIS INTACT, TACTICAL PRICE SIGNAL NOISY. ISM confirms copper/electrical-component scarcity, but recent LME squeeze dynamics argue against extrapolating peak spot prices. Aluminium scarcity remains a valid newer physical-market divergence; AA/CENX/Norsk Hydro stay research candidates rather than automatic promotions.
categoryChanges.Robotics / Automation: NO WAVE REORDER. Structured warehouse/fixed automation still commercialises first, followed by cobots/mobile manipulation, then industrial humanoids. New ACE Robotics and AiMOGA evidence reinforces that world-model/training-data limitations remain binding for humanoids despite rapid China shipment growth.
categoryChanges.Water / Cooling: UNCHANGED POSITIVE. Water availability increasingly affects data-centre siting, power generation and agriculture; ECL/MOD/XYL remain higher-quality diversified expressions. MWA/HWKN/Kurita remain research candidates with operating evidence.
categoryChanges.Agriculture / Resources: UNCHANGED SELECTIVE. Fertiliser divergence remains about feedstock economics rather than generic fertiliser inflation. CF/UAN remain cleaner nitrogen expressions than phosphate names exposed to sulphur inflation; CHE.UN remains differentiated acid/water-chemicals infrastructure.
categoryChanges.Healthcare / Metabolic: UNCHANGED. No new weekend evidence alters LLY/DXCM/MRK/MRNA/HIMS research standing; healthcare remains useful cross-cycle diversification but is not the main Power Stack macro driver today.
